newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso says plans to raise pulp prices.
newsitem.headline: Enso says plans to raise pulp prices.

text.p: Finnish forestry group Enso Oy plans to raise softwood pulp prices by about $50 per tonne to $630 per tonne from the beginning of October, an Enso official told Reuters on Monday.

"We are likely to raise," said Simo Pesola, managing director of Enso's Nordic Fibres A/S unit, when asked whether Enso would follow Swedish Sodra Cell's announcement last Friday that it would raise long-fibre pulp prices to $630 per tonne from the current $580 in October.
But Pesola said he was not sure whether higher pulp prices would hold in the current uncertain market situation.
"Demand has in principle been quite good, but there has been somewhat too much supply," he said.
Pesola said some North American pulp producers have also recently announced plans to up pulp prices.
Enso's annual pulp production is 2.6 million tonnes, about 650,000 tonnes of which is market pulp.
Representatives of Metsaliitto group's pulp arm Metsa-Sellu Oy and UPM-Kymmene said they were monitoring the pulp market situation and that they would raise prices if possible.
"We are selling our pulp at the market price. As we are not a market leader, we will not make any official announcements about prices," said Metsa-Sellu managing director Risto Kekki.
He said demand for pulp had been healthy during the summer, but he feared speculative buying.
"The summer months have been lively in pulp trade but we don't know how much stock-building there has been. It may all be a transfer of stocks," he said.
Metsa-Sellu produces about two million tonnes pulp a year, about 20 percent of which goes to the market, Kekki said.
Torsten Nykopp, vice president of pulp steering at UPM-Kymmene, said there is a wait-and-see sentiment on the pulp market.
"Price hikes may hold if they are supported by production stoppages," Nykopp said.
"We will not take any leading role here as we are a net buyer," he added.
